issues.description: The solution implementation declares attribute identifiers using snake_case (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods use camelCase identifiers (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). The problem statement and UML expect camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This naming mismatch in the solution will cause compilation errors and confusion for students trying to map the UML/template to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier naming consistent in the solution. Either rename the declared fields to camelCase to match the UML and the rest of the class (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or update the constructor and all methods to consistently use the snake_case field names. Prefer changing the field declarations to camelCase so they match the problem statement and the typical Java naming conventions.
